purpose: A plasma globe whose two strongest tendrils are the hands: the thick one lands on the glass at the hour, the thinner one at the minute, both with a hot contact spot, while dim ambient tendrils wander the rest of the globe.

accent.where: the two hand tendrils and their contact spots, one violet; the ambient tendrils are the same hue, dim

night.recipe: The lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes (the Vinyl precedent); the mat around it, visible on the square device, flips with --face-bg, and night dimming comes from the kiosk brightness. For a dark room the glow option pulls the halo in.

options.intent: full is the neon as designed; soft keeps the tubes and their white cores but pulls the halo in, the setting for a clock by the bed.

antiPatterns.rule: Never paint the neon or the stage with --face-ink or --face-bg
antiPatterns.why: the lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes, like the Vinyl record; the day ink is black and would vanish on it, so only the mat outside the disc reads --face-bg

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the still parts live every frame
antiPatterns.why: nine glow passes per stroke made the drafts cost 17 to 20 ms a frame at 1080; anything that changes at most once a minute goes through N.layer in src/apps/clock/neon/faces/plasma.ts or the Pi drops frames

antiPatterns.rule: Never let an ambient tendril land on the hour or minute angle
antiPatterns.why: the two hand tendrils are the only way to read the time; a third bright line near them makes the face unreadable from across a room

specless: Drawn on a canvas by src/apps/clock/neon/faces/plasma.ts in the shared 1000-unit space. Noise-driven tendrils and contact glows have no place in the spec vocabulary of solid hands and two tick rings, so the numbers live in the draw module.
